title: Convert the mixed number first
text: A mixed number has to become an improper fraction before you multiply. $$1\frac{1}{2}$$ means $$1 + \frac{1}{2} = \frac{2}{2} + \frac{1}{2}$$. A common mistake is to multiply only the fraction part $$\frac{1}{2}$$ by $$\frac{2}{3}$$ and drop the 1. Which improper fraction equals $$1\frac{1}{2}$$?

title: What is left in the denominator?
text: After canceling, both the numerator and the denominator are 1. A product of $$\frac{1}{1}$$ equals which whole number?

title: Worked solution
text: $$1\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{2}{3} = \frac{3}{2} \times \frac{2}{3} = 1$$. Common mistake: multiplying only the fraction parts, $$\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{2}{3} = \frac{1}{3}$$, and ignoring the 1. General rule: convert a mixed number to an improper fraction before multiplying, then cancel common factors and multiply what remains.
